assumed_parameters.source: docs/HARDWARE-MODELS.md local DRAM preset, capacity overridden for this test

limitations: Fabric: each compute->pool link is a FIFO byte server and the pool is a shared byte server (aggregate pool service never exceeds pool bandwidth).
Requests larger than local DRAM spill their overflow pages to the pool (swap_remote only); a spilled newest page makes each KV append a fabric write.
Closed-loop: the issuing request blocks until its transfer completes, so queue_depth_bytes backpressure is inherent; excess is still reported as queue_overflow_events / backpressure_stall_ns.
Percentiles come from a log-bucket histogram (upper bucket edge, <=1% relative error, never under-reports).
scenario_assumptions: Local capacity is intentionally set to 2 GiB to force overflow. A real H100 node has far more DRAM; this scenario exists only to exercise the remote path.
One compute node and one shared pool keep the event stream small enough to inspect by hand.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode derived from Llama-3-70B geometry, not a captured trace.
The compute tokens_per_second field is omitted, matching examples/llama-70b-cxl.json. Request duration is therefore driven by modeled memory accesses, not accelerator throughput.
